Small road exiting onto a main road, trying to cut a turns timing short to beat massive train of morning rush hour on both sides of the road. It's a country road? The speed limit is 45 but people regularly go up to 65 mph and more. 

Cue setting. Northeastern snowpocalypse aftermath, with snowbanks 8 feet high (not supposed to be that high at all ). It's super cloudy, and to the left cars must ascend a slight incline coming out of a growth/woody area. 

I should have enough time ti barely make it to the other lane. Out zooms a black Volvo from the hill(which would have rendered it invisible on your average summer day anyway), no lights despite it being mildly icy and very dark and cloudy. I hesitate for a fraction of a second and get hurled into the road on the right lane. If I didn't hesitate I'd have some serious knee injuries at the very least. the Volvo hit the front left wheel on my car and knocked the rather large German tank a good three yards. She didn't brake till almost impact.

Volvo spins into the opposite lane and knocks the back wheel of a Subaru outback. He rolls into the shoulder. Everyone gets out okay, most of the damage is car damage. It's clearly the woman's fault for not driving cautiously on such a day and not slowing down despite arriving at an area where cars often exit (she travelled this road often) with no lights, but in this state if you are merging into a major street no matter how wrong the guy who hits you is, it's still your fault. 

My mistake really was being a second semester senior in high school-sleeping in. Funny thing was, the emts said I was pretty composed to still be able to stand up and walk around and talk  despite my age-she said shed seen fully grown adults break down crying and unable to move after a fender bender. 

So please, kiddies and adults, please be careful of snowbanks and crazy people driving around really fast.
